_description: Controlled synonym dataset. Every entry is sourced from real, already-published corpus data (production/calculators/calculator-seo-map.json's own secondaryKeywords, or a calculator content file's own heroTitle) - none invented. Every entry carries type/confidence/source. Candidate pairs found in the source data but rejected as NOT real synonyms are listed separately in rejectedCandidates, with the reasoning, so the exclusion is auditable rather than silent.

synonyms.source: calculator-seo-map.json secondaryKeywords (cpa) - same formula (spend / conversions), a common alternate name rather than a formal acronym expansion
calculator-seo-map.json secondaryKeywords (aov) - AOV = revenue / orders, this is that formula in words
calculator-seo-map.json secondaryKeywords (cr) for 'Conversion Rate'; 'CVR' is the same metric's other common acronym, verified against no conflicting corpus usage
production/calculators/content/nrr.json heroTitle + calculator-seo-map.json secondaryKeywords ('net dollar retention calculator')
common notation variants of the same corpus-wide term - not from a single calculator record, applies site-wide (see search-typo-tolerance-contract in SEARCH-DESIGN-HANDOFF.md)

rejectedCandidates._description: Pairs the source data juxtaposes (as a related/co-searched keyword) but which are NOT the same metric - excluded per the task's explicit warning against fabricating semantic synonyms.

entries.reason: ARR = MRR x 12 - a related, derived metric, not the same quantity. calculator-seo-map.json lists 'arr calculator' as a co-searched secondary keyword for mrr, which is a relatedness signal (see search-relations.json), not a synonym.
A rate of change of MRR is a different metric (a percentage) from MRR itself (a currency amount) - listed as a secondary keyword for discoverability, not interchangeability.

Different denominator (Monthly vs Weekly active users) produces a genuinely different ratio and a genuinely different number for the same underlying DAU - calculator-seo-map.json lists 'dau/wau stickiness calculator' as an adjacent/confusable search term precisely because it's easy to conflate, not because they're the same metric.

Explicitly named as a non-synonym pair in this task's own brief - ARPU (Average Revenue Per User, typically per period) and LTV (a lifetime-horizon projection) answer different questions even though both are revenue-per-user metrics.

Explicitly named as a non-synonym pair in this task's own brief - CTR measures clicks/impressions, Conversion Rate measures conversions/visits (or /clicks) - different funnel stages, different denominators.
